learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge and application of environmental technologies and sustainability.
Recognize the pollutants that can be generated and the effect or impact they produce on the receiving medium (atmosphere, water, and soil).
Analyze an industrial activity and identify the environmental problems it may generate.
Plan a basic strategy for pollution prevention and control in specific cases, for water, air, and waste.
Select the most appropriate purification and/or pollution control technique in specific cases, as well as size effluent treatment facilities.
Know the basic related environmental regulations: discharges, atmosphere, waste, environmental impact assessment, integrated pollution control.
Understand the fundamentals of an Environmental Management System at a basic level.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities, and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the Industrial Technical Engineer profession.

Democratic values and sustainability. Develop a commitment to the society in which we live so that it prospers through the dimensions of democratic values and sustainability, materialized within the global framework that defines it at all times.

syllabus_topics: Topic 0. Introduction: Current environmental problems. Agenda 2030 and Sustainable Development Goals.
assessment_rules: Each assessment component requires a minimum score of 5 out of 10. If practicals or the practical project are not passed during the semester, they can be made up via a written individual test in the official calls. If the mid-term exam is not passed, the final exam will cover all course content and account for 70% of the final grade, also requiring a minimum of 5 out of 10. Students must be able to demonstrate authorship of their work in an oral interview, otherwise, the grade for those activities will be zero.
